channel.title: Auto Research Digest EN RSS
channel.description: A research publication on the design, approval, evaluation, and operation of LLMs, generative AI, and AI agents in real work.

item.title: When can a human approval become a rule for future agent tasks?
item.description: An invoice example explains when AI agents can reuse human approvals, with explicit conditions, exception tests, rule ownership, and expiry.

item.title: When to clarify a request and when to show an AI prototype
item.description: Use questions for missing requirements and prototypes for emerging preferences. Research and an outline example explain revision and verification.

item.title: Evaluating AI agent actions beyond the final answer
item.description: Evaluate AI agents using booking traces, approval order, tool arguments, and saved state. Learn how to allow valid paths and detect regressions.

item.title: Verifying AI data entry and saves in applications without APIs
item.description: Verify computer-use agents before and after Save. An invoice example covers duplicate prevention, managed desktops, and uncertain results.

item.title: What to verify when sales AI turns meeting notes into CRM updates
item.description: Check CRM update proposals from sales AI: opportunity matching, field evidence, changed records, and saved results, with product comparisons.

item.title: Choosing editable formats for AI-generated presentations
item.description: Compare images, SVGs, and chart objects in AI-generated slides, then test the next revision in PowerPoint or Google Slides.

item.title: How to compare permissions, approvals, and evaluation in agent platforms
item.description: Use a ticket-update task to compare agent platform permissions, approvals, traces, and evaluation, including responsibilities left to existing systems.

item.title: From an agent listing to an approved organizational trial
item.description: Separate agent discovery, connection, purchase, and distribution. Define permissions, costs, changes, and withdrawal for an organizational trial.

item.title: What to preserve so an AI agent can resume interrupted work
item.description: Distinguish saved sessions from task recovery using Managed Agents and Google ADK: persistence, artifact versions, duplicate actions, and resumption checks.

item.title: Reviewing a coding agent: plans, permissions, diffs, and tests
item.description: Separate coding-agent plan review, branch and VM isolation, Verified signatures, and test evidence to understand what each check establishes.

item.title: Designing agent memory for retrieval, applicability, and updates
item.description: Design agent memory around scope, current instructions, corrections, and concurrent writes, then evaluate retrieval and update failures separately.

item.title: Handling corrections, interruptions, and saved results in voice booking agents
item.description: Speech interruption does not undo a booking save. Compare voice architectures and coordinate corrections, API state, and call testing.

item.title: When to split AI work into subagents, and what they need to share
item.description: Decide whether subagents help by examining task dependencies, shared criteria, evidence handoffs, total cost, and comparison with a single agent.

item.title: What MCP, A2A, and AG-UI actually exchange
item.description: Use a refund workflow to separate what MCP, A2A, and AG-UI exchange for connection, delegation, and interface updates from application approval and execution.

item.title: Choosing video AI by reference inputs and revision work
item.description: Compare reference inputs, audio, and editing in Runway, Google Flow, and Adobe Firefly, then test a one-condition revision of the same clip.

item.title: Separating agent identity from delegated user permissions
item.description: Separate agent identity, user delegation, and downstream API permissions using Microsoft, AWS, and MCP examples for document search and external sending.

item.title: Delegating meeting preparation to Cowork: drafts, calendar changes, and review
item.description: Separate reading, draft saving, and calendar or delivery changes when delegating meeting preparation to Cowork, then design checks for each stage.

item.title: What chat and editing interfaces each contribute to AI work
item.description: Use Canvas, Pages, and Cocoa to decide where an AI interface should place requests, direct artifact editing, plan review, and approval.

item.title: Before releasing an agent, test what external instructions can make it do
item.description: Design pre-release agent tests that distinguish prompt-injection detection, tool-call authorization, and containment of outbound transmission.

item.title: Evaluate agent readiness against the work your organization must complete
item.description: Use public agent benchmarks to define workflow-specific completion, exceptions, retries, escalation, and review cost before rollout.
